title: Citroen Built A Rotary GS, Then Tried To Buy Them All Back And Crush Them - Carscoops
content:
One of just 847 GS Birotors is heading to auction, alongside the even rarer rotary prototype that started the whole adventure The 1970s rotary gold rush persuaded everyone from GM to Mercedes that pistons were old news. Citroen jumped aboard too, only to eventually decide its rotary GS was something it would rather forget. It even tried buying the cars back so it could destroy them. Related: Citroen’s Iconic 2CV Is Coming Back As A $17,000 EV Fortunately, some owners didn’t cooperate. One of the survivors is this 1973 GS Birotor being offered without reserve by Broad Arrow at The Quail Auction, where its $20,000 to $30,000 estimate makes it look suspiciously affordable among Monterey Car Week‘s seven-figure exotica. The regular GS was already wilfully unconventional, with slippery styling and Citroen’s famous hydropneumatic suspension. It was deservedly named European Car of the Year in 1971. But through Comotor, its rotary joint venture with Germany’s NSU, Citroen stuffed in a twin-rotor Wankel derived from the technology used in the NSU Ro 80. The 2.0-liter unit produced 105 hp (106 PS) and drove through a three-speed semi-automatic transmission. Unfortunately, the Birotor arrived just as the 1973 oil crisis made thirsty cars about as fashionable as narrow-leg pants. It was also enormously expensive, costing almost as much as Citroen’s grander DS. Just 847 were built before more conservative Peugeot took control of troubled Citroen and decided the rotary experiment wasn’t worth supporting. But the new bosses went further than merely axing the Birotor. Rather than keep supplying parts for a tiny population of troublesome cars, Citroen attempted to buy Birotors back and scrap them. Broad Arrow says roughly 250 are thought to survive today. This example formerly belonged to the Mullin Automotive Museum and shows an incredible 1,080 miles (1,740 km). But for Citroen geeks, this Monterey find gets even more tempting. Because Broad Arrow is also auctioning a 1970 M35 (see bottom two galleries), the road-going laboratory that preceded the Birotor. Its unusual Heuliez-built 2+2 body hides hydropneumatic suspension and a tiny 995 cc single-rotor Wankel. Citroen built only 267 M35s, loaning examples to selected customers who effectively became development drivers. It later bought back and destroyed many of those too. This Mullin Museum alumnus has covered 11,600 miles (18,704 km) and is estimated to fetch $30,000 to $40,000. So while collectors nearby fight over another million-dollar Porsche, you could conceivably spend around $50,000 and take home two incredibly rare survivors from one of Citroen’s wildest engineering dead ends. GS continues to strengthen its position in the global dealmaking landscape, with its latest merger and acquisition (M&A) league-table performance underscoring the depth of its investment-banking (IB) franchise. Goldman ranked the top financial adviser on mergers and acquisitions in South and Central America during the first half of 2026 by both deal value and transaction volume, according to GlobalData. The investment bank advised on three transactions valued at a combined $10.4 billion during the period. Notably, two of the three transactions were billion-dollar deals, helping Goldman maintain a sizable lead over peers like Morgan Stanley MS and JPMorgan JPM in terms of deal value. Investors have responded positively to Goldman's improving fundamentals, with GS shares gained 17.7% year-to-date outperforming the industry's average of 11.7%. Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan shares rose 21.3% and 11.7%, respectively, over the same time frame. With such strong momentum, investors may be wondering whether to buy GS stock now or wait for a better entry point. To help answer this question, let us take a closer look at the key factors driving Goldman's growth and assess whether the stock still has room to run. M&A advisory remains a key competitive strength for Goldman. Winning mandates on large transactions not only supports advisory revenues but can also generate opportunities across financing, underwriting and other client businesses. Recent league-table rankings highlight that strength. Goldman was the only adviser in South and Central America to exceed $10 billion in aggregate deal value during the first half of 2026, according to GlobalData. It also ranked first among North American M&A advisers by deal value, advising on $437.7 billion of transactions. The favorable M&A backdrop led Goldman to deliver strong results. GS's IB fees rose 52% year over year in the first half of 2026, driven by higher advisory, equity underwriting and debt underwriting revenues amid improving capital markets activity. Management also sounded constructive about the operating environment following the second-quarter results. CEO David Solomon highlighted accelerating momentum across the company's businesses and pointed to strong client demand for Goldman to advise on major strategic transactions. Management noted that the investment banking backlog reached its highest level in five years, including a record advisory backlog, supported by robust strategic M&A activity, AI-related capital formation and stronger financing demand. AI-Led Initiative to Transform Business: GS is undertaking an ambitious, firmwide artificial intelligence (AI) transformation aimed at boosting fee income, improving productivity and expanding long-term operating leverage. The initiative spans its core businesses, including trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations, positioning AI as a central growth driver. Last month, Yahoo Finance, citing Reuters, reported that Goldman Sachs Asset Management had launched AlphaAI, an artificial intelligence-focused investment platform. The initiative underscores the firm's conviction that AI will emerge as a significant driver of investment opportunities and returns across both public and private markets. Earlier, Goldman partnered with Anthropic on a $1.5-billion initiative designed to accelerate AI adoption across hundreds of portfolio companies. At the center of Goldman's transformation are two major initiatives — One Goldman Sachs 3.0, or OneGS 3.0, and the GS AI Assistant program. OneGS 3.0 is a multi-year effort to integrate AI into the firm's core operating model rather than treat it as a standalone technology. The program focuses on simplifying workflows, modernizing infrastructure and supporting scalable growth through shared platforms, standardized processes and higher-quality data. The GS AI Assistant is expected to further improve employee productivity by helping professionals analyze information, generate content and complete routine tasks more efficiently. As adoption expands, the platform could reduce manual workloads and allow employees to devote more time to client engagement, decision-making and higher-value activities. Management has expressed strong confidence in AI's long-term potential. Although spending on AI, data and digital infrastructure may keep expenses elevated in the near term, the investments could generate meaningful productivity gains and help the firm move toward its medium-term efficiency ratio target of 60%. Strategic Streamlining Pays Off: The company's streamlining efforts have been underway for some time as it retreats from the underperforming consumer banking ventures. Under CEO David Solomon, GS has embarked on a deliberate transformation to exit non-core consumer banking and double down on the divisions wherein Goldman maintains a clear competitive advantage. In sync with its restructuring efforts, in April 2026, the company acquired Innovator Capital Management, expanding its active ETF capabilities as part of a broader strategy to build durable revenue streams through diversified asset and wealth management offerings.  In the same month, Goldman completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski, further streamlining its asset management operations. In the third quarter of 2025, the company transitioned the General Motors credit card program. These moves demonstrate a well-thought-out exit, allowing the company to reallocate capital and attention toward higher-margin, more scalable businesses like Global Banking and Markets, and the asset and wealth management divisions. Robust Liquidity Aids Capital Distribution: GS maintains a fortress balance sheet, with the Tier 1 capital ratios well above regulatory requirements. This financial strength allows it to return capital to its shareholders aggressively through buybacks and a healthy dividend yield. As of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $187 billion, while deposits totaled $558 billion. Total unsecured debt (comprising long-term and short-term borrowings) was $438 billion, of which only $90 billion was near-term borrowings. Following the Federal Reserve's 2026 stress test, the company increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share beginning in the third quarter of 2026. The company also has a share repurchase plan in place. In the first quarter of 2025, the board approved a share repurchase program of up to $40 billion of common stock. As of June 30, 2026, Goldman had $21.6 billion worth of shares available under authorization. Including dividends, GS's total return over the past three years has been 206.3% compared with the industry's average of 132.3%, and JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley's averages of 132.5% and 146.6%, respectively. Thus, the combination of potential capital appreciation, dependable dividend income and continued share repurchases enhances the stock's total-return prospects. Supported by Goldman's robust liquidity and capital levels, its shareholder payout activities appear sustainable. Analysts are bullish on GS. Over the past 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings has been revised upward. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Goldman's 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 34.2% and 4.9%, respectively. The GS stock currently trades at a premium to the industry. The stock is trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) of 14.58X above the industry average of 14.08X. Its peers JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are trading at a P/E of 14.41X and 16.63X, respectively. Goldman is well-positioned to benefit from stronger capital markets volumes and a record IB backlog. Its leading M&A franchise, rising IB fees and upward earnings estimate revisions further support the growth outlook. The company's focus on AI, productivity and strategic streamlining should also strengthen long-term profitability. By exiting less attractive businesses and prioritizing higher-return Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management operations, Goldman could improve earnings quality. Its strong capital and liquidity position also supports continued dividends and share repurchases. Though GS valuation looks expensive, this premium appears justified by the company's leading M&A position, improving earnings outlook and strong execution. Overall, the GS stock appears to be a compelling buy for investors with a medium- to long-term horizon. Although the stock's strong recent performance may lead to periodic volatility, any meaningful pullback could offer an attractive entry point for investors seeking exposure to a premier global investment-banking franchise. We're talking about 10 such bikes, ranging from touring bikes with Japanese reliability to adventure bikes that excel at everything. There's something for everyone here. This list is organized in descending order of pricing. BMW offers the best of two-wheeled luxury, comfort, and performance with the K 1600 GTL. This full dresser brings the best of "big" American luxury charm with sophisticated technology to offer a surprisingly versatile land yacht. A unique six-cylinder engine powers the K 1600 GTL. This 1,649 cc mill produces 160 horsepower at 6,750 RPM and 132.7 pound-feet at 5,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual coupled to a final shaft drive system. For the chassis, a cast-aluminum bridge-type frame is present. It is suspended on BMW's famed Duolever front suspension with a central spring strut and 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets the Paralever setup, coupled to a cast-iron single-sided swingarm and 5.3 inches of travel. Technology features are galore, too. Notable ones include a huge 10.25-inch TFT, a four-button cluster for custom functions, dynamic traction control, three ride modes, dynamic electronic suspension, hill start control, heated grips and seats, and an audio system, among others. This is arguably the most value-packed luxury touring motorcycle, and it undercuts the Honda Gold Wing, despite being more powerful. The 1,649 cc mill mentioned above is present here as well, in the same exact tune. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual and a final shaft drive neatly hidden in its single-sided swingarm. The chassis is also similar to the GTL, featuring the bridge-type cast aluminum frame. As for suspension, the front gets a double-wishbone (Duolever) with 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a monoshock (Paralever) setup with 5.3 inches of travel. The suspension offers electronic adjustability and even an automatic load-leveling feature. There is no dearth of top-spec technology. The K 1600 B gets a huge 10.25-inch TFT with a wide range of connectivity and integrated map navigation features. Other notable features include three ride modes, dynamic traction control, hill start control, and engine brake control, among others. This futuristic-looking touring bike makes luxury feel practical. The same boxer twin powers the R 1300 RT as on the go-anywhere R 1300 GS. The 1,300 cc mill produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM, sent to the wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. Underpinning the R 1300 RT is a two-part frame with the engine utilized as a stressed member. It is suspended on BMW's famed Telelever front and Paralever rear suspension setups with 5.8 inches of front and 6.2 inches of rear travel. Adding to its versatility is a factory-adjustable seat, solid wind protection, and commendable technology. Notable features include keyless ride, dynamic electronic stability control, heated grips, and a gorgeous-looking 10.25-inch TFT with Bluetooth navigation as standard. This BMW adventure bike is famed for being a flagship that can do it all exceptionally well. Powering the flagship GS is the 1,300 cc liquid-cooled mill, which produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a standard six-speed manual with a final Cardan shaft drive system. It can also be equipped with an optional automatic transmission. Underpinning the R 1300 GS is a sophisticated setup. It comprises a pressed-steel main frame utilizing the engine as a stressed member. It is suspended on a double-wishbone suspension setup up front with 7.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a link-type monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. BMW has loaded the R 1300 GS to the brim with technology features. Notable ones include four ride modes, dynamic traction control, dynamic brake control, dynamic cruise control, and hill start control. The dashboard comprises a sizable 6.5-inch TFT. The BMW S 1000 RR is a surprisingly affordable sports bike that is cheaper than a Honda Fireblade. Powering the S 1000 RR is a proven inline-four engine that produces 205 horsepower at 13,000 RPM and 83 pound-feet of torque at 11,000 RPM. It is coupled to a WSBK-derived quick throttle as standard as part of its latest update. Underpinning the flagship BMW sportbike is a lightweight twin-spar aluminum frame, coupled to a race-derived aluminum swingarm and subframe. The frame is suspended on 45 mm inverted front forks with 4.7 inches of travel, alongside a monoshock with 4.6 inches of travel. Both ends offer full adjustability. Cutting-edge technology such as six ride modes, pit lane limiter, launch control, dynamic traction control, wheelie control, and slide control is present, too. This BMW crossover feels worth every dollar because it blends urban mobility, highway runs, and even spirited mountain sessions so seamlessly. The S 1000 XR packs a proper superbike engine derived from the S 1000 RR. The 999 cc liquid-cooled inline-four mill produces 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox. Underpinnings comprise a bridge-type cast aluminum frame, using the engine as a load-bearer, suspended on long-travel springs. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 5.9 inches of travel, and the rear comprises a monoshock with 5.9 inches of travel. Its electronic, self-adjusting rebound settings at both ends instill sharp cornering confidence. Technology features are plentiful and stitch its do-it-all character together. This is BMW's arch-nemesis to the Triumph Scrambler 1200. The R 12 G/S is powered by a mighty 1,170 cc boxer twin engine with 109 horsepower at 7,000 RPM and 85 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. The engine sits in a tubular space frame and is suspended on long-travel suspension. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 8.2 inches of travel, and the rear gets a monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. Both ends are fully adjustable. This is further complemented by durable aluminum cross-spoke wheels wrapped with all-terrain tires. The R 12 G/S gets a slew of assistive technology features. Notable ones include riding modes, dynamic traction control, cornering ABS, dynamic engine brake control, and partial integral brake system. This classic cruiser bike matches the essence of American big twins but with a unique twist: a large air-oil-cooled boxer-twin engine instead of a V-twin. In fact, it is the largest production motorcycle flat twin until the much-anticipated production-spec R 20 breaks cover. The 1,802 cc mill produces 91 horsepower at 4,750 RPM and 120 pound-feet of torque at 3,000 RPM. Adding to its heavy-duty outlook is a double-loop steel main frame with bolted beams. A twin-sided steel swing arm is part of the chassis and adds to its stretched-out stance. The R 18 gets telescopic forks up front with 4.7 inches of travel. The rear comprises a hidden monoshock that seems to be strongly inspired by the Harley Softail series. Owing to its old-school charm, BMW has added very little technology to the R 18, with notable features being LED lighting and a USB Type-C port only. This is a gravely overlooked BMW naked bike that offers grin-worthy performance at a bargain price. It is powered by the same 999 cc inline-four liquid-cooled engine as the S 1000 RR, but subtracts the ShiftCam for a more peaky output of 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a standard slipper clutch. The chassis components are also S 1000 RR derived, featuring inverted 45 mm forks up front with full adjustability and 4.7 inches of travel and a fully adjustable monoshock with 4.6 inches of travel. With a curb weight of as low as 432.1 pounds, the power-to-weight ratio is commendable on this Beamer. The S 1000 R is further tamed with a slew of top-spec electronics, such as M Quick action throttle, engine drag torque control, and three riding modes. BMW also packs a TFT display with smartphone connectivity as standard fitment. This BMW adventure bike balances ruggedness, comfort, and versatility. The F 900 GS takes flight in the heated middleweight segment and shines bright. A versatile 270-degree parallel-twin engine powers it. This liquid-cooled 895 cc mill produces 105 horsepower at 8,500 RPM and 68.6 pound-feet of torque at 6,750 RPM. As for the chassis, ​​​​​​​you get a bridge-type main frame coupled to a steel bolt-on subframe and a cast aluminum twin-sided swingarm.​​​​​​​ This is coupled to 43 mm inverted front forks with full adjustability and 9.05 inches of travel. The rear gets a monoshock with preload and rebound adjustability and 8.46 inches of travel. To match its go-anywhere attitude, it gets a 21/17-inch spoked wheel combination wrapped around all-purpose tires. The technology suite is stacked with notable features like dynamic traction control, a standard Akrapovic sport muffler, rain and road riding modes, heated grips, and a 6.5-inch TFT with Bluetooth connectivity. title: NewPrinces Restructures Retail Operations Around GS Brand - ESM Magazine
content: Italian retail and food conglomerate NewPrinces Group has initiated a restructuring of its retail operations, placing the historic GS supermarket brand at the heart of its business strategy. Effective 1 August 2026, the group consolidated its corporate structure by merging GS and Princes Retail into Princes Property, which the company subsequently renamed GS. The move follows NewPrinces' entry into the large-scale retail sector in 2025 through its acquisition of Carrefour Italia, which Princes Retail previously managed. Along with the corporate merger, NewPrinces unveiled a revamped corporate identity featuring a modernised GS logo. The strategic shift represents a core pillar of the group’s strategy of creating an end-to-end supply chain that unifies production, logistics, and retail distribution under one roof, while consolidating its relationship with end customers. Over the coming months, GS plans to roll out a phased renovation project across its retail network. The company’s footprint currently encompasses approximately 1,000 stores across Italy, including around 750 franchised locations. It has roughly 10,000 direct employees and 8,000 franchise staff, as well as physical storefronts alongside online grocery services and a growing omnichannel model. NewPrinces reshaped the brand's signature oval logo into a complete circle, which its says reflects the company's fully integrated supply chain and its goal to serve as a daily staple for Italian consumers. President Angelo Mastrolia commented, "The GS logo embodies an important history and a bond built over time with millions of customers. This is why we have chosen to retain its most recognisable elements: not a change from the past, but rather the desire to enhance a heritage that continues to be relevant today. “An identity capable of uniting past and future, maintaining a strong relationship with those who knew GS and embracing new generations.” Thanks! please check your email to confirm your subscription. title: GS Holdings’ Q2 operating profit surges 253% on strong refining margins - Korea JoongAng Daily
content: GS Holdings posted a 253.4 percent surge in second quarter operating profit as stronger refining margins, higher oil prices and robust lubricant earnings lifted results above market expectations. GS Holdings reported a 253.4 percent surge in quarterly operating profit for the April-to-June period on year upon higher international oil prices and rising export prices for petroleum products. The company on Tuesday reported an operating profit of 1.71 trillion won ($1.21 billion) for the second quarter of 2026, beating the market consensus of 1.12 trillion won, compiled by market tracker FnGuide. The holding company, which owns oil refiner GS Caltex, also reported increases in both revenue and net profit. Quarterly revenue rose 24.9 percent year on year to 7.41 trillion won, while net profit surged 1,180.5 percent to 1.13 trillion won. Compared to the first quarter of 2026, revenue rose 8.3 percent from 6.84 trillion won, operating profit increased 36.5 percent from 1.26 trillion won and net profit climbed 36.9 percent from 826.7 billion won. For the first half of the year, GS's operating profit was reported at 2.98 trillion won, up 130.8 percent from the year prior. Revenue rose 17.2 percent and net profit jumped 415.6 percent during the same period. GS attributed the sharp improvement in its consolidated second quarter results largely to strong earnings at GS Caltex. “This was driven by wider refining margins amid higher international oil prices and export prices for petroleum products, as well as a temporary inventory effect,” GS said. “In particular, the lubricants business posted record-high earnings due to global supply disruptions.” It added that operating profit from GS Energy’s resource development business also increased on the back of higher oil prices. The petrochemical business, however, swung to an operating loss from the previous quarter as higher naphtha costs were not fully reflected in product prices, according to GS. Its power generation subsidiaries — GS EPS and GS E&R — also posted weaker results due to lower system marginal prices and operating rates. “Oil prices are expected to remain volatile in the third quarter due to developments in the Middle East, while the temporary inventory effect is also expected to fade,” the company said. “How flexibly we respond to these uncertainties will affect our performance.” Ryoo Sang-dai, whose three-year term ends Aug. 20, said earlier lessons impel the central bank to take a pre-emptive monetary policy response. Price pressure from demand- and supply-side factors affecting export-led growth and higher oil prices on the back of the Iran war may force the bank's hand. Employment insurance subscribers aged 29 and under declined for a 47th straight month in July, highlighting worsening job conditions for young Koreans.

title: GS Q2 Operating Profit Soars 253% to 1.7 Trillion Won on Refining - Seoul Economic Daily
content: Refining Swings to 2.2 Trillion Won Profit; Petrochemicals Slip to 6.3 Billion Won Loss GS (078930.KS) posted second-quarter operating profit more than three times higher than a year earlier, driven by a strong performance in its refining business. Operating profit on a consolidated basis reached 1.72 trillion won ($1.24 billion), up 253.4% from 486 billion won a year earlier, the company said on the 11th. Revenue rose 24.9% over the same period to 7.41 trillion won. For the first half, cumulative revenue climbed 17.2% to 14.26 trillion won, from 12.16 trillion won a year earlier. Operating profit for the period jumped 130.8% to 2.98 trillion won. GS attributed the sharp improvement in second-quarter results to strong earnings at GS Caltex. High oil prices in the second quarter fueled a surge in temporary inventory gains, while supply disruptions at overseas petrochemical producers widened refining margins on key products. GS Caltex swung to an operating profit of 2.55 trillion won in the second quarter, reversing a loss from a year earlier, while revenue rose 55% to 16.67 trillion won. By segment, the refining business swung to an operating profit of 2.20 trillion won. As persistent geopolitical risk in the Middle East and concerns over global supply disruptions kept prices rising — with Dubai crude climbing to $96 a barrel in the second quarter — spreads on major petroleum products such as gasoline, kerosene and diesel widened sharply. The lubricants business also benefited from higher prices amid supply concerns, posting operating profit of 357.7 billion won, up 213% from a year earlier — a record high. The petrochemicals business, however, swung to a loss from the previous quarter as product prices failed to keep pace with rising naphtha costs. The segment recorded second-quarter revenue of 2.69 trillion won and an operating loss of 6.3 billion won. Power generation subsidiaries also turned in weak results, hurt by lower system marginal prices (SMP) and reduced utilization rates. A GS official said the outlook remains uncertain heading into the third quarter. "Oil price volatility tied to the Middle East situation will persist, and the temporary inventory effect is expected to disappear," the official said. "How flexibly the company responds to this uncertainty will affect its results." Original reporting by Jung Hye-jin for Seoul Economic Daily. AI-translated from Korean. title: Karol G’s new album may just have you crying at the club - Gulf Today
content: It may be summertime, but Karol G is unapologetically leaning into her sadness. On Friday, the Colombian pop star released her seventh studio album “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto,” a 14-track project that details the depths of heartache one can only access when finally tuning out the world. Tinged with dream-pop accents and acoustic instrumentation — though still fringed with her signature reggaeton-pop flair — it is a dramatic departure from her previous album, “Tropicoqueta,” a lofty, genre-rich album that envisioned a Latina-led utopia as a tropic floral paradise. Now, with “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto” — which in English translates to “I Don’t Regret Feeling So Much” — Karol G swaps her vibrant, tropical facade for a soft blue vulnerability. Her special new brand of perreo melancolía features guest vocals by Drake (who sings in Spanish), Bruno Mars, Greg Gonzalez (of Cigarettes After Sex), as well as Spanish stars Judeline and Rusowsky. The melodrama begins early on with the opening track, “Te Llevas To” — a moody EDM elegy that explores the loss of one’s self after a relationship ends. In an interview with Elle magazine, the hit maker shared that she spent a lot of time alone when creating this project, following her split from Colombian singer-songwriter Feid late last year — long before headlines caught wind of their breakup in January. “Everything started when I went to Hawaii [last November]. I did a lot of hiking alone. I would climb the mountains alone. I would stand there gazing at the sky. I learned a lot about enjoying my solitude in this industry — we are really, really lonely. Compared to the rest of the world, you’re very isolated,” said Karol G in the Elle interview. Rumblings of the new project first surfaced in April when Karol G performed at the 2026 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival as its first Latina headliner. There, she debuted “Después de Ti,” a shoegaze ballad joined by Greg Gonzalez, front man of the indie-pop band Cigarettes After Sex; the song expressed profound grief after Karol experienced a loved one’s death. “I cry a lot. I’m super sentimental and I’ve hated myself a lot for that,” Karol G revealed to Elle in her July cover story. “But at the same time, I’d rather suffer because I lived too much — because I loved too much, because I had too much fun — than to not have had those experiences, you know? I’m inviting everyone to be a little more dramatic, a little more extra.” Although her classic bichota essence — a term Karol G frequently uses to describe herself, as a female counterpart to the Puerto Rican bichote, or “big shot” — is still heavily present in the new LP. Earlier this summer, Karol teased the song “Matadora” during the opening night of her international stadium tour in Chicago; produced by reggaeton pioneer Tainy, the sultry track is hallmarked by a muffled jazz trumpet and suggestive verses for an unknown paramour. Her longtime collaborator, Colombian record producer Ovy On The Drums, also returns to incorporate elements of Karol’s Grammy-winning 2023 album, “Mañana Será Bonito,” which followed her public breakup with ex-fiancé Anuel AA and grew into a massive commercial hit. With Ovy, Karol revived the shadowy timbre of her joint Shakira track “TQG” into the new “Bebiendo Lágrimas,” a reggaeton song that adamantly rejects the notion of love. Mexican American producer Edgar Barrera — who previously worked with Karol on her merengue smash “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido,” as well as “Mi Ex Tenía Razón” and “Gucci los Paños” — reprises his role as a música mexicana connoisseur, aiding in Karol’s synth-doused Tejana-style cumbia, “Alguien Que Te Amaba.” (The track was also written with legendary songwriter Pete Astudillo, who co-wrote many of Selena Quintanilla‘s greatest hits.) In the anguished “Con Quien Andara,” the singer pays tribute to the Spanish singer-songwriter Jeanette and her hazy, sentimental pop ballad from 1976 titled “Porque Te Vas?” And if that’s not enough of a nostalgia bomb, there’s the dream-pop reggaeton track “Bby Wow,” which features Judeline and Rusowsky and was inspired by the popular 2003 dancehall track, “Coolie Dance Rhythm” by Cordel “Scatta” Burrell. (Millennials may also recall echoes of this sample in popular tracks like Nina Sky and Jabba’s 2004 “Move Ya Body.”)

title: GS Caltex drives GS profit surge on higher oil and export prices in South Korea - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz

GS Caltex's second-quarter revenue was 16.6724 trillion won, up 55% from a year earlier. Operating profit was 2.5507 trillion won, swinging to a profit from a year earlier. Operating profit in the lubricants institutional sector was 357.7 billion won. Looking only at the lubricants institutional sector, revenue rose 52% and operating profit increased 213% from a year earlier. GS Caltex's refining institutional sector results also improved. In the refining institutional sector, second-quarter revenue was 13.2965 trillion won and operating profit was 2.1993 trillion won; revenue rose 59% from a year earlier and operating profit swung to a profit. Compared with the first quarter, revenue increased 28% and operating profit rose 44%. However, GS Caltex's petrochemical institutional sector turned to a loss from the previous quarter. The reason was that the increase in naphtha prices could not be fully reflected in product prices. Power generation subsidiary GS EPS posted weak results due to the second-quarter average system marginal price (SMP) falling 4% year over year to 118 won. GS EPS recorded second-quarter revenue of 209.0 billion won but an operating loss of 7.3 billion won. Even looking only at revenue, it fell 14% from a year earlier and 48% from the previous quarter. A GS official said, "In the third quarter, oil price volatility stemming from the Middle East situation is expected to persist, and the temporary inventory effect is also expected to disappear," adding, "How flexibly we respond to uncertainty will affect results."

title: GS Corp. Posts Q2 Operating Profit of 1.7174 Trillion Won, Up 253% Year-on-Year - 아시아경제

GS Corp. Posts Q2 Operating Profit of 1.7174 Trillion Won, Up 253% Year-on-Year GS Corp. reported that its operating profit in the second quarter of this year more than tripled compared to the same period last year, fueled by strong performance from GS Caltex driven by higher refining margins and temporary inventory effects. The lubricants business also posted its best-ever results, supported by improved profitability amid global supply disruptions. On August 11, GS Corp. announced that its consolidated revenue for the second quarter of 2026 reached 7.4131 trillion won, with operating profit at 1.7174 trillion won and net profit at 1.1320 trillion won. Compared to the previous quarter, revenue increased by 8.34%, operating profit by 36.45%, and net profit by 36.93%. The improvement was even more pronounced compared to the same period last year. Revenue grew by 24.93%, operating profit surged by 253.37%, and net profit jumped by 1,180.54%. As a result, GS Corp.'s cumulative revenue for the first half of this year was tallied at 14.2555 trillion won, with operating profit at 2.9760 trillion won and net profit at 1.9587 trillion won. Compared to the first half of last year, revenue rose by 17.22%, operating profit by 130.82%, and net profit by 415.58%, respectively. The strong performance of GS Caltex was the main contributor to the improved results. Increased international oil prices and export prices of petroleum products have expanded refining margins, while temporary inventory effects further enhanced profitability. In particular, the lubricants segment posted record-high performance due to global supply disruptions. The resource development segment of GS Energy also saw increased operating profit, supported by rising oil prices. On the other hand, the petrochemical segment turned to a loss compared to the previous quarter, as it was unable to fully reflect the increased naphtha prices in final product prices. Power generation subsidiaries also posted sluggish performance in the first half of the year due to declining SMP (system marginal price) and operating rates. A GS official said, "In the second quarter, GS Caltex delivered strong results thanks to higher refining margins and inventory effects resulting from increased international oil prices and export prices of petroleum products. The lubricants business also achieved record-high performance due to global supply disruptions, and GS Energy's resource development segment saw higher operating profit supported by rising oil prices." The official added, "In the third quarter, oil price volatility is expected to continue due to tensions in the Middle East, while temporary inventory effects may disappear. title: Cicero, MMR Split Up From Pilot Challenge GS Points Lead - dailysportscar.com
content: ShareFacebook, Twitter, Google Plus, Pinterest, Email IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge GS Championship leader Nate Cicero has parted ways with McCumbee McAleer Racing (MMR) and announced an indefinite hiatus from motorsport with only three races left in the 2026 season. Cicero, a member of the 2026 Ford Racing Driver Development Team, joined MMR’s Pilot Challenge programme midway through the 2025 season and helped the team capture its first Michelin Pilot Challenge victory last year at Road America. After helping co-driver Jenson Altzman secure fourth in the 2025 GS (Grand Sport) standings, Cicero joined undefeated Mustang Challenge North America champion Robert Noaker for the 2026 campaign. Through seven races, the drivers of the #13 Ford Mustang GT4 combined for three podium finishes, and a best finish of second at Watkins Glen. After last week’s race at Road America, those results gave Cicero and Noaker a 100-point lead in the GS (Grand Sport) standings. On 6 August, Cicero abruptly announced his departure from the sport, saying: “I will be taking a leave from racing to focus on personal matters and would appreciate privacy at this time. I want to thank everyone who supported me over the years.” Five days later on 10 August, MMR released its own statement regarding Cicero’s departure. “We are disappointed to announce that our relationship with Nate Cicero has come to an end. Effective immediately, Nate is no longer associated with MMR in any capacity. We will have no further comment on the topic,” the team said. “We remain focused on moving forward and continuing to build on MMR’s goals and success. As we look to our future, we will be making a driver announcement in the coming days.” Ford Racing was also approached by DSC and declined to comment. As a child in karting ten years ago, Cicero was mentored by MMR co-owner Stevan McAleer and his brother Stuart. Cicero’s affiliation with MMR continued into his graduation to the Whelen Mazda MX-5 Cup, where he took Rookie of the Year honours in 2023, finished sixth in the standings, then improved to fourth in 2024. That is the mantra for Head Coach Nick Hart's Gibson Southern High School Football Titans entering the 2026 season. In 2025, the Titans posted a 12-2 (6-0 Pocket Athletic Large-School Division) season that featured PAC Large-School Division, two victories over No. 1-ranked teams IHSAA Class 3A Sectional 32 and IHSAA South Regional championships before falling just shy on the road against eventual IHSAA Class 3A State Champion Cascade in the 3A South Semi-State. Following graduation of a highly successful group of seniors, Hart looks for the Titans’ Class of 2027 seniors to lead a relatively inexperienced to varsity football team that, following the program’s Maroon-and-Gold game at Jack Jewell Memorial Field Aug. 8, hosts Evansville Central Aug. 14 in an IHSAA preseason scrimmage ahead of the Titans’  season opener, a non-conference home game Aug. 21 against Class 5A-affiliated Floyd Central, which won the IHSAA Class 5A Sectional 16 title a year ago. The Titans are ranked No. 2 in the 2026 Indiana Football Coaches Association Class 3A preseason poll. “This is a really-fun group to coach, and I thought that we had a great week one (of official practice),” said Hart of the Titans’ preparations. “They’re a group that has fun competing and getting after it, and they enjoy it. They’re a highly-motivated group that I’ve not had to ask them to get going even one time. They’ve really attacked this first week, which is great." “Even though we graduated a bunch of guys, we also have guys stepping up into new spots. I thought we did some good things on both sides of the ball,” said senior OT Ben Reinhart following the Maroon-Gold game. “Our defense came up with some interceptions, and we scored some touchdowns. We still have some things to work on, but I thought we played pretty hard.” “Overall, I think our defense played really well,” said senior DT/DE Khale Campbell after the intrasquad scrimmage. “We have some minor things to work on that we’ll learn from and fix. The offense competed and went as hard as they could today, which really helped the defense get better. Overall, I think it was a really-good Maroon-and-Gold game.” “We still have a lot that we need to fix, clean up and get better at,” Hart added, “but we don’t have to ask this group to play hard. They’ve got that piece, and we work on and fix the things that we need to. We’ve got to keep getting better and fix some of the mistakes we’re making, but I feel like we’re ahead of where we thought we would be at this point of the season, so that’s always a good thing. With our schedule (which begins with playing 2025 5A Sectional Champion Floyd Central in Week 1 and Missouri powerhouse St. Pius X in Week 2 in the United Fidelity Bank Bowl), our guys are going to have to be ready to go right away.” “All summer, we’ve been working hard, and I thought we had a pretty good week one,” said Reinhart in describing the Titans’ preparations for the season ahead. “We’ve really been getting after it and competing throughout the summer and through week one,” added Campbell. “Yes, we graduated quite a few guys, but guys are working hard to step up and fill those roles. We’ve just got to continue to fight and improve so that we can be ready for Week 1.” As for this year's seniors, “They’ve exceeded my expectations, and they’ve really set the tone for our football team,” noted Hart. “They just go and attack every day and give it everything they have. Our seniors have done a really-great job so far.” Senior QB Caden Rochleau (22-for-41; 261 passing yards; 4 passing TD, 4 INT; 158 yards rushing, 1 rushing TD as a junior), after filling in for Wabash College football signee Zach Foster (197-for-310; 2164 yards passing, 29 TD passes, 10 INT; 1061 yards rushing; 9 rushing TD as a senior) following Foster’s injury in the regional championship game, made his first-career varsity start in the 2025 South Semi-State championship game and is set to fully take the reins of the Titans’ offense. “I couldn’t be more proud of Caden,” said Hart. “He’s stepped up and kind of taken that role head-on. He’s got all the talent in the world, and he’s done a great job of taking care of the football throughout the whole summer. I thought that in our first offensive drive (of the Maroon-Gold Game), he was surgical in the passing game and in the RPO game. He made great decisions and was getting the ball to where it needed to go. He was running our offense very well and very clinically. His understanding of the position, and his decision-making, continues to grow and progress.” “Caden’s really been getting after it all summer,” noted Reinhart. “He’s continued to step up and grow. He’s really committed to putting the work in and doing the best he can for our team so that we can be as successful as possible.” “Caden was thrown into a tough position (following the injury to Zach Foster), but he’s really worked his tail off to earn the position,” noted Campbell. “I’ve definitely seen growth in him. He’s determined, and he wants to win and help lead the team. It’s definitely a good mindset to have.” At running back, the Titans look to veteran backs in senior Eli Foster (378 yards rushing as a junior) and junior Tucker Deputy (274 yards rushing; 5 rushing TD as a sophomore) to fill the production provided by Hanover College football signee Colin Scherer (835 rushing yards; 14 rushing TD; 11 catches, 90 receiving yards as a senior), though Deputy has also transitioned into more of a role in the Gibson Southern linebacker corps. Others to watch include sophomore Makade Malone. “I think we’ve got a really nice stable there,” said Hart. “Eli brings a lot of experience and runs hard, and Makade Malone brings a speed factor to the backfield, and then we have Tucker, who ran it some last year. He’s more on the defensive side of things now, but we have the ability to bring him over, as well. We have three really-good guys back there to run the football for us.” “I think our run game has been solid so far,” added Reinhart. “Eli’s been pretty good, and he gives us a ton of experience in that spot. Overall, I think our running-back room is looking pretty good, which gives us confidence as an offensive line.” “I’m really happy Eli is there in the backfield,” said Campbell. “He’s a great fit at that position, and we feel confident that the rest of the room will continue to step up and grow.” With graduation of key contributors such as WR Noah Kuester (57 catches, 640 yards receiving, 13 TD receptions), WR/H-Back Toby Pullum (38 catches, 333 yards receiving, 6 TD receptions), WR Jake Mazzier (23 catches, 208 yards receiving, 1 TD reception) and WR Lloyd Sellers (28 catches, 394 yards receiving, 4 TD receptions), the Titans’ leading returning receiver is senior Peyton Johnson (42 catches; 483 yards receiving; 5 TD receptions as a junior). “Peyton’s had a great summer,” noted Hart. “He’s a guy that kind of gives us an A.J Brown-ish kind of receiver. He can take the top off of the defense and go get it, but as a big, strong, guy, he can break tackles and also give us those tough yards on the outside after catching hitches and curls.” Others to watch for in the receiving corps include juniors Ayden Bodrie and Luke Mallory, as well as senior Elijah Ortiz, junior Isaac Dill and junior Austin Smith. “Ayden and Luke are both very athletic and do a good job of going up and catching the football,” said Hart. “We’re looking to see who emerges and how that rotation works itself out.” “I feel like our receiving corps is going to be explosive and exciting this year,” described Reinhart. “They’ve all got big-play ability, especially with Caden’s arm strength. Peyton is back, and he was a big piece of our offense last year. We have a lot of guys competing for spots, which will be good for our team.” “Overall, I think our receivers are ready,” added Campbell. “Peyton is back, which is a big help. All the guys competing for those spots are ready to go.” While the Titans graduated three-fifths of last year’s offensive-line starters in LT Spencer Staggs, LG Blake Ulm and C Bobby Robinson, Gibson Southern returns starters in junior RG RJ Smith and senior RT Owen O’Neal to a new-look quintet in the trenches. Senior Ben Reinhart, who split time between tight end (5 catches, 39 yards in 2025) and defensive end (12 total tackles; 1 tackle for loss; 1 pass break-up - ahead of the Semi-State) as a junior, made the transition to serving as a full-time offensive lineman and looms at left tackle. Hart noted that competition is ongoing between the trio of Nathan Emery, Eli Bodrie and Jadyn Kiefer to determine who will emerge with the additional starting positions on the offensive line. “We’re continuing to get better there every single day,” said Hart. “Our pass protection is probably ahead of our run game at the moment. Over the next couple of weeks, we have to keep focusing on getting better up front in the run game. We had a couple of nice plays today, but we need to be able to run the football more efficiently and effectively than where we are after week one (of official practice).” “We graduated three guys on the left side of the line,” noted Reinhart, “but we get RJ and Owen back, which is huge for us. I kind of knew that I would be making the switch to the offensive line ahead of time. We also have a bunch of new guys that are hungry and looking to step up and earn those spots.” “The people that have filled in have stepped up to (try and) earn those positions,” added Campbell. “Guys are continuing to compete and fight for their spots. With who we have on the O-Line now, I feel like those guys are ready to go.” Following graduation of a senior-laden defense that featured Lindsey Wilson football signee and four-time All-State DT Brody Klem (65 total tackles; 28 TFL; 7 sacks; 1 forced fumble - ahead of the Semi-State), MLB Colin Scherer (116 total tackles; 10 TFL; 4 PBU; 2 INT; 2 fumble recoveries - ahead of the Semi-State) and DB Lloyd Sellers (state-leading 10 interceptions in 2025), the Titans look to a returning senior starter on each level in DT Khale Campbell (50 total tackles; 17 TFL; 5 sacks - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior), LB Ian Maikranz (66 total tackles; 3 TFL; 1 INT; 4 PBU - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior) and S Cole Ridens (59 total tackles; 4 PBU - ahead of the Semi-State - as a junior) to lead the way for a new-look group on that side of the football. Others competing for defensive-line spots alongside Campbell include senior DT Gavin McEllhiney, junior DT Isaac Peach, sophomore DE Lincoln Plasse and sophomore DE Reed Luecke. “It’s been great competition,” noted Reinhart of the Titans’ offensive and defensive lines competing against one another. “Iron sharpens iron, as I like to say. We push each other to play hard and make positive strides every day. We have guys on the D-Line that are hungry and looking to make an impact.” “We have some decent size up front, but I think overall as a defense, we’re a lot more athletic, maybe, than what we usually are,” noted Hart. “That’s something that really stands out. Those guys are really able to run around and chase things down. As a whole, our defense flies around and makes plays. It’s a group that I’m really excited about. This is a group that, throughout the summer and through week one, has been able to run the ball particularly well on us. We still have some work to do, but our front-seven has done a really good job of playing the run so far.” “We have some younger guys on the line,” noted Campbell, “but they have the right mindset of doing what it takes to win. We’ve been attacking every day in practice, and we’re ready to just go, go, go.” As for the Titans’ linebacker corps, “Ian played outside last year, but we’ve moved him to ‘Mike’ this year, and he’s done a great job in there,” noted Hart. “He’s been the quarterback of the defense for us and gets us where we need to be. “Tucker Deputy has moved over from running back, and then junior Gabe Foster and junior Max Brink are competing, as well,” Hart added. “As a whole, our linebackers have played really well. I really like where we are there in terms of athleticism. That group is possibly as athletic a group that we’ve had there in a while from a strength and speed standpoint. They do a great job of flying around.” “Ian has stepped up, and that group as a whole is really going and competing on every play,” noted Campbell. “They’re doing their jobs well and getting their jobs done.” “Those guys are battling every day and continuing to get better,” said Reinhart of the linebacker corps. The Titans’ secondary team is battling through various injuries ahead of the 2026 campaign, said Hart. “It’s been a mix-and-match type of thing there so far,” Hart said. “Cole Ridens is back as a starter at safety, and Elijah (Ortiz) played a lot of safety last year, as well. Having two guys at safety with that level of experience is huge.” At cornerback, “Isaac Dill started a couple of games last year,” added Hart. “(Junior) Eli Stone and (junior) Kaigan Nossett have also done a fantastic job so far. We’ve got a little depth there. “As a whole, and as a team, there are some guys that have stepped up over the summer and through this first week that we weren’t sure were going to get there,” Hart said. “We have to keep building competitive depth across the board, especially with the way that we want to play. A lot of guys have continued to step up and work hard as we go into the season.” “I’m really proud of those guys. The guys in the secondary are really competing and fighting to earn their spots,” noted Campbell. “I feel like we’re pretty strong in the secondary.” Rochleau returns as the team’s punter, but the competition for the remainder of the Titans’ special teams’ positions is ongoing following the graduation of senior PK Will Redden (59-for-61 PATs, 3-for-5 FGs in 2025), a three-sport All-Gibson County athlete a year ago (football, soccer and golf), as well as Mazzier, a Western Kentucky University Baseball signee and the 2025-26 Princeton Clarion Gibson County Male Athlete of the Year, who played a key role in the return game in 2025. Hart noted that Jeter Simmons, a Princeton Clarion All-Gibson County and All-Pocket Athletic Conference performer on the soccer pitch, looms as the team’s kicker in filling that role in a similar fashion to what Redden did a season ago. “Jeter is new to us, and he had a good day today (Saturday at the Maroon-Gold Game), where he didn’t miss one, which I thought was great” noted Hart. “For a guy that’s never really kicked before (on the football field), he’s really been consistent throughout the opening week. He’s come out and has done a great job." “Jeter’s stepped up and earned that position,” noted Campbell. “He’ll be ready to go.” “Caden’s got a great leg as our punter,” shared Hart. “He’s an athletic guy, and it’s always good to have a guy that is as athletic as him as your punter. He did a great job last year, and he’s continued to do a great job so far there.” Lincoln Plasse, who has been “really consistent so far here, early in the process,” said Hart, looms as the team’s long snapper, while Elijah Ortiz looms as a candidate to return punts, while Isaac Dill and Makade Malone loom as potential candidates as kickoff returners. Special teams “is something that we spend a lot of time on and want to be good at, although it’s maybe the toughest thing to simulate and get a good live look at at this point of the year,” said Hart. “We won’t fully know what we have there until we get into that Week One game. content: GS Shop said Tuesday that demand for fruit-and-vegetable juices has surged amid the prolonged summer heat. As fresh produce prices climb, juices — relatively affordable and easy to store — are drawing attention as a substitute food option. GS Shop has been expanding its juice product lineup since last year to meet that demand. With health-conscious consumers in their 40s and 50s — the platform's core customer base — adding to the trend, juice order values rose 279 percent in June and 244 percent in July compared with the same months last year. Per a recently released Goldman Sachs report, “Global M&A volumes rose 48% YoY against an unusually supportive backdrop,” which was “driven primarily by the surge in deal size, with mega M&A volumes +125% YoY.” And the firm expects that strength to continue, saying that the M&A cycle has “substantial room to run, despite long-standing geopolitical and inflationary pressures.” Further, we’re witnessing a historical IPO market (which is great for the underwriters), as the recently completed second quarter saw nearly $116 billion in IPO proceeds (largely driven by the SpaceX IPO), which marks the second-highest quarterly total this century, behind only the first quarter of 2021 (at $133 billion). Should dealmaking continue apace, and should we see the much-anticipated IPOs of Anthropic or OpenAI emerge, it looks like the environment should remain supportive for investment banks. With that in mind, let’s take a look at two of Wall Street’s heaviest hitters when it comes to dealmaking: Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS). MS has been the better performer over the last year, rising 49.5% compared to 43.5% for GS. But over the last five years, Goldman Sachs has handily outperformed the competition, with a 151.2% gain compared to Morgan Stanley’s 106.9% increase. That said, both stocks are trading just off their all-time highs, so if you were inclined to give the round to MS, I wouldn’t argue. While dealmaking fees are independent of an investment bank’s book of assets, P/B is still a reality check for banks. On that lens, GS looks less stretched than MS. MS offers a modestly higher dividend yield, but if your 2026 thesis includes “higher-for-longer rates plus decent equity returns,” that extra yield can be meaningful—especially if deal volumes don’t accelerate as quickly as hoped. MS is more popular among institutional investors, who hold meaningfully more of the “float” (publicly available shares) than they do in GS. But that can cut both ways, as it suggests deep sponsorship and broad index/fund participation (often supportive in drawdowns) but can also mean more “crowding” (less incremental buyer power and more selling “ammunition” if sentiment flips). Goldman Sachs is the 800-pound gorilla when it comes to investment banking and is routinely at the top of the heap when it comes to total volume. In the first half of 2026, Goldman advised on an astronomical $1.3 trillion in deals (per this scorecard from dealogic), which put them well ahead of Morgan Stanley’s $880 billion. That follows a 2025 in which Goldman was also at the front of the pack ($1.6 trillion in deals vs. Morgan Stanley’s $1.1 trillion), and a similarly weighted 2024 ($968 billion for Goldman; $744 billion for Morgan Stanley). These are both heavy hitters, but Goldman leaves the competition in the dust, and when advisory and underwriting activity rises, the bank that’s already winning the biggest mandates tends to capture a disproportionate share of the incremental fees. And that’s especially important this year, which has seen an increase in the number of large deals and a decrease in the number of smaller mergers. Both are elite, but the market exposure isn’t identical: So even if both banks continue to participate in the 2026 surge, GS gives you more exposure to the thesis. Both companies should do well in a deal-heavy environment, and they’re both “Bull Market Stocks” (as Mike Cintolo would put it), but if you’re looking to play the M&A and IPO boom in 2026, Goldman Sachs gives you the most upside. *This post has been updated to reflect current market conditions. title: VB-G RAM G’s first month shows sharp fall in rural jobs: Jairam Ramesh - The Tribune
content: "The first month of the Modi government's VB-G RAM G scheme is already bringing to light the cost of dismantling MGNREGA," Ramesh said. Welfare& Unemployment He said the figures vindicated concerns raised by the Congress and other Opposition parties when the government replaced MGNREGA with the new legislation. "The core spirit of MGNREGA was to free workers from dependence on the whims and mercy of the government of the day," he said. Drawing a contrast with VB-G RAM G, Ramesh alleged that the new scheme had centralised implementation, placed a greater financial burden on state governments and made access to employment increasingly dependent on technology and biometric authentication. He further alleged that the new framework had removed the employment guarantee and made it more difficult for rural workers to claim their entitlements. Ramesh said the nearly 50 per cent decline in workdays generated under the new scheme during its first month showed the impact of the changes. "This is exactly the situation that the Congress and the entire Opposition had warned about when the Modi government bulldozed MGNREGA," he said. Calling the new scheme "outright employment theft", Ramesh alleged that the government's policy was weakening a legal safeguard that had provided rural households with access to employment during periods of economic distress. title: Fans Choose Karol G’s Album ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’ as Best New Latin Music of the Week - Billboard
content:
The album earned more than 60% of the vote in the latest Billboard New Music Latin poll. Karol G has topped Billboard’s new music Latin poll published on Aug. 7 with her sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. Billboard readers voted for the 14-track set as their favorite music release of the week after the New Music Latin poll and playlist was published; the album earned more than 62 percent of the vote. In contrast to her vibrant and tropical-leaning Tropicoqueta — which debuted No. 1 on Top Latin Albums and No. 3 on the all-genre Billboard 200 in 2025 — NMADST is a more intimate, vulnerable look at the Colombian artist, who’s embracing her feelings and emotions. Sonically, the set is powered by heart-wrenching ballads, as well as dreamy glam pop, reggaetón, electronic and Afrobeats. On the album, Karol brought in star-studded collabs including Drake on the kizomba-influenced “Ahí”; Bruno Mars on the ‘80s power love ballad “Still”; and Judeline and Rusowsky on the dancehall tune “Bby Wow.” “I’ve always been open to making music in other languages — without pressure, as long as it flows and happens organically and naturally — and, well, that song found me,” the “Bichota” singer expressed of her collab with Bruno in a Tiktok on Aug. 7. “It expressed exactly what I was feeling and how I was feeling it; it was literally perfect for what I was going through, and I listened to it constantly. I tried to overthink it, but it was perfect — I hope it touches many people’s hearts.” Another fan favorite in this week’s New Music Latin poll — following Karol’s winning album — is Ryan Castro and Feid’s third collaborative effort, “Mentira.” See the full poll results below. title: LS Electric, GS E&C Partner on DC Power Distribution for AI Data Centers - thelec.net
content: LS Electric and GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C) have agreed to collaborate on direct current (DC) power distribution technology and power equipment supply for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. LS Electric said on Aug. 10 that it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with GS E&C to jointly respond to changes in the AI data center business environment. Under the agreement, the companies will develop next-generation DC power distribution technologies aimed at improving power efficiency in high-power, high-density AI data centers. As part of the partnership, LS Electric will supply key electrical equipment for AI data center projects being developed by GS E&C, including switchboards, gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) and extra-high-voltage transformers. LS Electric is currently developing DC power distribution products such as solid-state transformers (SSTs), solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs) and energy storage systems (ESS). The company has also established a production facility at its Cheonan site in South Chungcheong Province that operates entirely on a DC power distribution system. An LS Electric official said demand for DC power distribution technologies is increasing as operators seek to improve the power efficiency of AI data centers.

title: Mailbag: Vikings Night Practice Offers Unique Start to Preseason Opening Week vs. Giants - Minnesota Vikings
content:
Do you have a comment or question? Send it to the Mailbag. Every Monday we'll post several comments and/or questions. Click here to submit a comment or question to Mailbag. Remember to include your name and town in the email. If Twitter / X is your jam, you can send a question to me that way as well. The annual night practice of Vikings Training Camp was held Sunday, providing an enthusiastic introduction to Minnesota's first week of the preseason, which will culminate at noon (CT) Saturday when the Vikings visit the Giants for both teams' first preseason game of 2026. Players are off today and will return to action Tuesday, the first of three days of practices, before flying to the New York area Friday. That also means that an unofficial (you can bold that word, underline or highlight it, or do all three) depth chart is likely to be unveiled this week ahead of the preseason opener (if history holds true). Be on the lookout for that, and make sure to tune in for Saturday's game, which will air in the Twin Cities market on KMSP FOX 9. Because of the timing of the night practice and the perpetual camp to-do list, this Mailbag will be a little shorter than most. View photos of Vikings players during Training Camp Night Practice on August 9 at TCO Stadium. Training camp is on, and everyone's spirits and expectations are high across the league. Players, coaches and the NFL fanbases are all excited. This was how I felt last August. Then a number of injuries and re-injuries to the O-line had me asking my brother if a team has ever drafted all offensive linemen in a draft before. I know some fans want to blame all struggles on QB and injuries there, which was part of it, but a protected QB in an O'Connell offense will burn any defense in the league with Jets and Jordan Addison on the field. We saw Sam Darnold crumble under exotic pressures against the Lions and Rams (twice each), and we've seen the same for his multiple replacements. I honestly think the 2026 Vikings will go as far as their O-line takes them. Based on camp so far, is there a position or group we should be more worried about or keyed into? How has Blake Brandel looked at center? Chances of getting any other veteran depth at center or guard before the season starts? Cheers to Brian O'Neill and his new contract. I hope our trenchmen stay happy and healthy throughout the season. Skol! The lack of continuity at QB in the 2023 and 2025 seasons has been a big talker, especially when compared to the results the team put together in 2022 and 2024 when the starter was able to go the full season. But the B-topic that provides context and nuance that many on social media and/or TV do not have time for was just how rough a go the o-line had in 2025, which counteracted the Vikings best-laid plans for a second-year QB coming off missing his rookie season with a knee injury. There were just 83 snaps played together by the intended starting five of Christian Darrisaw, Donovan Jackson, Ryan Kelly, Will Fries and O'Neill, and there were 26 combinations across the five positions. Kelly was a four-time Pro Bowler with the Colts who was brought in to lead the rebuilding of the interior of the line, a mission essentially declared by Head Coach Kevin O'Connell from the podium after Minnesota's Wild Card loss to the Los Angeles Rams that was moved to Arizona. Unfortunately, Kelly was only able to play at least 50 percent of the team's offensive snaps just five times. The Vikings turned to second-year pro Michael Jurgens and Brandel, who played the pivot for the first time ever but has built on those learning experiences this offseason. We'll have a feature on Brandel in the coming days. The first-team offensive line of Darrisaw, Jackson, Brandel, Fries and O'Neill has looked good at redefining the line of scrimmage on multiple run plays. We haven't seen Demond Claiborne highlights. Is he hurt? And what is going on with the punter battle? This email was received early last week. Claiborne had been limited slightly for part of camp, but by the end of last week, he was really starting to flash. The most recent example is fresh after the sixth-round pick executed a tremendous jump cut and zipped through the line. Receiver Marcus Sanders, Jr., sealed cornerback Marcus Allen, a fellow undrafted rookie, and began jogging beyond Claiborne. The play popped for a 60-yard rushing touchdown for a team that is trying to add more explosive plays in the run game. Friday's extended practice, the longest of camp to-date, offered the first extended looks at Vikings punters Johnny Hekker and Brett Thorson. Vikings.com's Rob Kleifield covered that part of practice in that day’s observations. We also heard from Special Teams Coordinator Matt Daniels on Saturday. The convenient timing allowed for an update from Daniels. I see Jamal Adams as a chess piece in Brian Flores' defense. He is a linebacker and a safety. He can play the way Harry the Hitman played. Can you imagine the opposing QB trying to get a read with Joshua Metellus and Adams on the field at the same time? This will be fun. How important is academic achievement in recruiting and drafting offensive lineman? Brian O'Neill — All-ACC Academic Team. Donovan Jackson — BS and strong family academics. Joe Huber — mechanical engineering. Walter Rouse — biomechanical engineer. Caleb Tiernan — four-time Academic All-Big Ten. Delby Lemieux — honor society at Dartmouth. I have left out many more academic-orientated offensive linemen vying for spots on our team. It really seems like we value brains and braun when recruiting offensive linemen. Adams has quickly made an impression on teammates and coaches. We've posted a few stories during his short time so far, mentioning his involvement in Friday's session, as well as his thoughts on switching to No. 32 after opening camp in No. 54. The switch provides Minnesota the option of lining Adams up at safety or linebacker. As news of the Adams signing broke, my immediate thought was the potential of adding some redundancy behind Metellus in the hybrid role, but there could be some times when both are on the field together. The latter noted how much he's enjoyed welcoming Adams as a teammate and confessed to watching Adams' early career highlights in the back of a lecture auditorium when he was a student at Michigan. That offers a unique lead-in to the second question from Gerald, and a reminder that O'Connell and others have iterated the desire to find "smart, tough players who love the game of football." There are certainly multiple types of intelligence, and it can require considerable bandwidth to handle the complexities of football. Quarterbacks have the most on their plate of any position, but centers also have quite a bit they are tracking, depending on which player sets the protection. Some systems use code words to help quickly relay information; some play calls are quite verbose and run the risk of getting lost in translation. Gerald pointed out numerous recognitions for offensive linemen, and they aren't nearly the only linemen on Minnesota's roster who have garnered academic awards and attended prestigious schools. What a player can do on the field always will be the biggest part of the evaluation, but evaluators also can learn more about a player's study habits, and academic success in addition to the rigorous athletic requirements for players could be an indicator of good study habits. Somewhat related, O'Connell was asked about rookie Max Bredeson's and highlighted the fullback's comprehension as a factor that has helped him open camp so strongly. "Since he got here, obviously the mental approach, his ability to — I mean, there's different types of players, right? And there's very few that can sit in a meeting room, don't need walk-through reps, don't need a rep of it to then start applying their own high-level awareness that we know they have, but sometimes it takes a little time, depending on the position. He's already shown he can apply that," O'Connell said. "And then I think it's been great seeing the physical side of it because you just never know from a standpoint of the different types of runs we're doing. You guys have seen it. We're asking him to do a lot of different alignments and movements and things like that, and then he's still able. He's always been really good getting fit in space on blocks, but he's also been a really physical presence for us to help get runs started." title: GS E&C, LS Electric join forces to boost AI data center competitiveness - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Engineering & Construction announced Monday that it has partnered with LS Electric to strengthen its competitiveness in the AI data center business. The two companies signed an MOU for "joint response to changes in the AI data center business environment" at LS Yongsan Tower in Yongsan-gu, Seoul. GS Engineering & Construction CEO Heo Yun-hong, LS Electric Chairman Koo Ja-kyun and LS Electric CEO Chae Dae-seok were among the attendees. Under the agreement, the two companies will work together to navigate the rapidly changing AI data center market and technology landscape, and cooperate to ensure the smooth execution of related projects. The partnership will establish a framework for GS Engineering & Construction to receive timely supplies of key power equipment for its current and planned AI data center projects through LS Electric. The arrangement is expected to enhance the stability and execution competitiveness of the AI data center business, widely regarded as a key growth driver. AI data centers require higher power density and cooling performance than conventional cloud data centers due to the large-scale operation of high-performance computing equipment such as GPUs. Large-scale power intake and reliable substation and distribution infrastructure are considered core elements of AI data center projects. The two companies also agreed to jointly explore next-generation power solutions to keep pace with the technological shift from cloud to AI data centers. Specific areas of cooperation include holding technology exchange sessions on modular data center and direct-current distribution-based power solutions, jointly addressing the design and technical requirements of major customers such as global big tech companies, and collaborating on the supply of power equipment for AI data center projects. "Power infrastructure competitiveness is the key factor that determines the success or failure of an AI data center project," a GS Engineering & Construction official said. "Through this agreement, we will continuously strengthen our AI data center competitiveness by jointly addressing not only power equipment supply but also next-generation power solutions and the technical requirements of global customers."
